def: The difference between how a model change moves an offline eval score and how it moves the production metric it is meant to predict.
Rank correlation computed from concordant and discordant pairs, \(\tau=(C-D)/(C+D)\). More stable than Spearman with few releases.
One minus the fitted slope of online delta on offline delta. A shrinkage of 0.4 means online moves are about 60% of offline moves.
Leave-one-out prediction of each past release from all others, used to estimate how well an offline suite predicts the next release.
The share of past releases where offline and online deltas agreed in sign. The number that matters for ship decisions.
An online experiment with the same model in both arms, used to measure the noise floor of the online metric.
The pull of a regression slope toward zero when the predictor is measured with noise, as offline deltas are.
Benchmark items, or close paraphrases of them, appearing in a model's training data, which inflates its score on that benchmark.
Removing training documents that overlap with evaluation items, usually by long n-gram matching, before training.
A unique random token embedded in an eval set so that it can be filtered from training data and detected if a model has memorised the set.
Re-running a benchmark with names, numbers, or option order changed. A large drop relative to a clean control suggests memorisation.
A membership-inference signal that averages the lowest-probability tokens of a text; seen text tends to score higher (Shi et al., 2023).
A benchmark that only counts items created after a model's training cutoff, so they cannot have been memorised.
The state where top models approach a benchmark's ceiling, so remaining differences are dominated by label noise and the benchmark stops separating models.
The software that sends tasks to a model, collects and scores outputs, and records results. The measuring instrument for every eval number.
A retry backoff drawn uniformly between zero and an exponentially growing cap, so retries from a failure burst do not arrive in lockstep.
Upward bias in a pass rate when retried tasks effectively get more than one draw at the answer, making them scored like pass@k rather than pass@1.
A hash over everything that can change a model output (task, prompt text, model id, sampling parameters, harness and judge versions), used to reuse results safely.
A task whose score varies across runs at fixed settings. Quarantined and reported separately rather than averaged into the headline.
A fixed order of checks (is it real, where is it, what else changed, errors, replay, read outputs) for deciding whether an eval drop is noise, measurement, infrastructure, or model.
A slice's share of the total score change, \(n_s \bar d_s / N\). Rank slices by this rather than by percentage change.
